subject: Design: access proxy + SAML service account migration for Private Control Plane
messages:
From: Tom Hart <tom.hart@nimbuscloud.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME Security <security@acmecorp.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private CP: SAML access + migrating service accounts

Hi Marissa,

We're preparing to onboard Redwood Private into our VPC and have a couple of identity questions that came up from our security and platform teams. Right now we have several long-lived service keys used by batch jobs and CI that authenticate directly to the control plane. For compliance we'd like to move to short-lived credentials driven by SAML assertions from our IdP (OneLogin).

High-level asks:
- Do you have a recommended pattern for bridging SAML group assertions into short-lived roles for the private control plane?
- Can we avoid internet egress from our VPC when exchanging assertions? Our security team prefers an in-VPC broker/proxy if possible.
- What's the recommended SCIM workflow for provisioning service-account objects versus human users?

We're aiming for a migration window in late August and want to capture design constraints before we open a formal RFC. Can you propose an approach and a checklist?

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Hart
Senior Platform Engineer, NimbusCloud
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Hart <tom.hart@nimbuscloud.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private CP: SAML access + migrating service accounts

Tom — thanks for the clear summary. TL;DR: we recommend an "access-proxy" pattern that sits in your VPC (customer-managed) and performs SAML assertion handling + short-lived token exchange with the Private Control Plane.

Why this pattern?
- Keeps assertion handling inside customer network (no egress of raw credentials).
- Lets customers control wafer-level network policies (NACLs, security groups).
- Enables mapping of IdP groups -> Redwood IAM roles via a lightweight translation table that the proxy can cache.

Key components we'll propose:
- Access proxy (customer-deployed container or small VM) that: accepts SAML responses, verifies signatures, queries SCIM for service-account attributes (optional), and calls Redwood's token-broker endpoint to mint short-lived tokens (15m–1h) scoped to an IAM role.
- SCIM sync from IdP -> Redwood to create service-account identities (if you prefer to provision service accounts centrally).
- Migration helper to rotate away long-lived keys (agent that can do gradual rollout by token type).

Dev/Laura/Priyom: can you draft a technical sequence and a short migration checklist (network ports, TLS pinning, SCIM attributes we need, role mapping example)? I'll share with Tom and Nimbus security for sign-off.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Hart <tom.hart@nimbuscloud.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 10:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private CP: SAML access + migrating service accounts

Folks — attaching a draft design and the ACL mapping spreadsheet (attached). Summary of the technical flow and migration steps below.

Attachment: acl-mapping.xlsx (contains example IdP group -> Redwood role mappings)

Design summary (access-proxy pattern):
1) Assertion flow:
   - Service/process obtains SAML assertion from corporate IdP (either via backchannel or headless SAML flow).
   - Access-proxy (deployed in customer's VPC private subnet) receives assertion via HTTPS (mTLS optional).
   - Proxy validates signature, checks audience and authn instant, and optionally introspects group claims.

2) Token issuance:
   - Proxy calls Redwood Private Control Plane token-broker API over the private peering link / private endpoint (no internet egress required).
   - Request includes: signed assertion (or signed JWT from proxy), requested role, requested TTL, and a short-lived proxy client cert.
   - Token-broker validates the proxy client credentials, validates assertion/claims, applies role-mapping rules, and issues a short-lived bearer token scoped to the requested IAM role.

3) SCIM provisioning:
   - For service-account objects we recommend using SCIM v2 with a dedicated service account in the IdP that writes to Redwood's SCIM endpoint.
   - Minimum attributes: externalId, displayName, groups, metadata {owner, environment, automated-job-id}.
   - SCIM-created service-account objects are mapped to a stable internal id used in audit logs.

4) Key security controls:
   - Short TTLs (<=1h) + rotation are required; no permanent keys should be used post-cutover.
   - Token-broker enforces MFA-for-admin-roles if requested by Nimbus.
   - Audit logs capture SAML assertion thumbprints + token issuance events, stored in your VPC logging endpoint via our log forwarder (optionally delivered over private peering).

5) Network considerations:
   - Access-proxy: outbound egress only to Redwood Private Control Plane private endpoint on port 443. If using peering, proxy traffic remains within the provider fabric.
   - Health checks: allow internal load balancer health probes between proxy and customer ALB on 8443.
   - Optionally restrict proxy to a small set of egress IPs that Redwood will register (for non-peered customers).

Migration checklist (proposed):
- Inventory: list all long-lived keys and owners. (Owner: Nimbus)
- Mapping: create ACL mapping spreadsheet (see attached). (Owner: Marissa/Dev)
- SCIM: enable SCIM provisioning for service accounts and test create/read/update. (Owner: Laura)
- Proxy: deploy access-proxy in staging VPC, configure certs, validate end-to-end issuance. (Owner: Tom)
- Canary: enable proxy for <10% of jobs, monitor error rates and latency. (Owner: Nimbus SRE)
- Cutover: rotate remaining keys and decommission old keys after 72h stable. (Owner: Nimbus Security)

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do you want the proxy to sign requests to Redwood with a customer-managed private key (recommended) or use mTLS mutual auth?
- TTL defaults: 15m vs 60m. Shorter TTL means higher rotation but less blast radius.

Next steps: please review the attached XLS and comment. I'll add a draw.io sequence diagram if folks want visual flow.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
